text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Retail store group KBB is seeking a major takeover in a non-core sector. (p1)
- Traffic and economic affairs ministries to probe possible illegal cross-subsidies of PTT Telecom KPN. (p1)
- Insurer Stad Rotterdam takes over remaining shares in rival De Amersfoortse to form new holding ASR Verzekerings groep. (p1)
- Philips Electronics is to sell nine units from its industrial electronics division. (p3)
- Unknown party bids for Leiden-based biotech firm MoGen . (p3)
- Dairy coop Coberco may have to close its plant in Zwolle after losing Nutricia unit Milupa as a customer. (p4)
- Activated carbon producer Norit's U.S. subsidiary takes 49 percent stake in Mexican rival Clarimax. (p4)
- Cooperative banking/insurance group Achmea not considing a bourse listing as has no plans for a large takeover. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- European aircraft industry seen conspiring against a possible relaunch of bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker. (p2)
- United Biscuits' unit Verkade targets at tighter organisation and new products with increased added value. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Minister Hans Dijkstal threatens to crack down on fighting between Kurds and Turks in the Netherlands. (p1)
- Shareholders lobby group VEB criticises practice of firms buying their own shares to boost the companies' value. (p13)
- Dutch businesses prefer to deal with German businessmen, according to an inquiry. (p13)
TROUW
- Speculation the biggest threat to the start of the single European currency Euro. (p5)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Agricultural minister Jozias van Aartsen considers a ban on pig breeding to fight spread of swine fever. (p1)
- Electronic cattle market, initiated by the five largest Dutch cattle markets, is to start officially this Friday. (p11)
